name: Tyabb
intro: Tyabb is the Peninsula's antique town and, twice a year, its airshow town, and for the rest of the calendar it is a small Western-Port-adjacent farming village most visitors drive past on the way to somewhere else. The antiques district is unusual  -  a long shed-filled lane known as Tyabb Packing House, half barn, half market, full of dealers who have been there for thirty years and know exactly what they have. The Old Tyabb airfield, a working grass strip on the edge of town, hosts the Tyabb Air Show each March and is home to one of Australia's best-known warbird collections. Beyond those two anchors, Tyabb is residential and rural  -  horse paddocks, a small main street, a bakery worth pulling over for. Come for an antique-hunting day with the airshow if the timing aligns; otherwise pair Tyabb with Hastings as a Western Port-side day.
factualLede: Tyabb is a small town on the Mornington Peninsula's northern Western Port flank, 65 km from Melbourne, anchored by the Tyabb Packing House antiques district and the Tyabb Air Show held at the grass airfield each autumn.

tldr: Tyabb has two anchors most visitors don't know about - Tyabb Packing House, the Peninsula's antique district, and the Tyabb Air Show on the grass airfield.
Best for: antique hunters; aviation enthusiasts; anyone building a Western-Port-side day with Hastings.
Signature experience: a half-day at Packing House, lunch at the bakery, then the air-show grass strip if the date aligns.
Half a day; pair with Hastings or Crib Point for the full Western-Port loop.
Train-accessible on the Stony Point line - a rare carless option for an antiques day.
notFor: first-time Peninsula visitors with one day
signature: The Peninsula's antiques district and grass-strip airshow town - two reasons to take the back road.
skip: Assuming there is nothing here - Tyabb Packing House alone earns the detour.
bestDay: Coffee on the main street, three hours at Tyabb Packing House, bakery lunch, then on to Hastings for fish and chips on the pier.
insiderNote: Time a visit around the Tyabb Air Show in early March - the warbirds in flight are the headline, but the Packing House the day before is open and well-stocked.
